title: A new provider returns null where the contract promises a quote and rejects an operation the contract requires

consumerGuidance.architecture: Nullable reference types are enabled solution-wide. IShippingQuoteProvider documents a non-null quote and requires tracking support from every registered provider.
consumerGuidance.notes: CheckoutPricing sums quotes from all registered providers. TrackingController queries every provider for a shipment reference.

mustCite: the null return from GetQuoteAsync against the non-null ShippingQuote declared by IShippingQuoteProvider
the consequence of a NullReferenceException for any basket with no nearby store, which the annotations do not prevent
a correction that keeps the declared contract, such as returning an unavailable quote or narrowing the declared return type deliberately
TrackAsync throwing NotSupportedException although the contract requires tracking from every registered provider
the consequence that one unsupported provider fails the whole tracking request
a correction addressing the concrete problem, such as separating the tracking capability from the quoting contract or excluding the provider from tracking queries

forbiddenFindings.example: Recommending that every interface method be split into its own single-method interface as a general rule.
Requiring a base class, decorator or CQRS handler for shipping providers.
Objecting to the sealed modifier, file layout or naming.

notes: Mirrors the guide's third calibration example. Nullable annotations are enabled, which is what makes the null return a contract break rather than a style question.
